ops.text: Concurrent codex-ask lanes SIGTERM-die with empty logs; sequential lanes are fine. 2026-07-18, P1 vault workflow: three codex-wrapper lanes dispatched CONCURRENTLY (wiring, manifest, flip-prep) all died at exit 143 with 0-byte reply AND log files — the underlying codex exec never wrote a byte. Pattern per the wrappers' own forensics: the initial codex-ask exceeded the 600s Bash foreground timeout → auto-backgrounded → each subsequent --await call itself timed out and was backgrounded → one of those SIGTERMs propagated to the codex child's process group and killed it. The two SEQUENTIAL review lanes in the same workflow (finder, refuter) completed normally. Mitigations that worked: run codex lanes one at a time from a workflow (chain them in one async thunk), and prefer a single long await over stacked 600s foreground awaits. Worth a real fix in codex-ask: detach the child from the await callers' process group so an await timeout can never kill the run.
